newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iranian police seize 368 kg of drugs.
newsitem.headline: Iranian police seize 368 kg of drugs.

text.p: Iranian police seized 368 kg (810 lb) of drugs in the central province of Yazd over the past 10 days, raising to 887 kg (1,955 lb) the amount of drugs seized in the province this month, the official Iranian news agency IRNA said.
IRNA quoted the head of Yazd province law enforcement department, Colonel Masha'allah Faraj-Poor, as saying six kg (13 lb) of the drugs had been concealed in the stomachs of the smugglers.

According to Iranian law, possession of five kg (11 lb) of opium or 30 grams (just over one ounce) of heroin is punishable by death. More than 1,000 people have been executed in drug-related cases since the law took effect in 1989.
Iran is a key transit route for drugs, mostly opium from which heroin is made, being smuggled to Europe via Turkey from Afghanistan and Pakistan.
